column3: It repeats the decisive image of coming to God with a sound heart and directly defines its saving significance.
The preceding exclusion of wealth and children supplies the judgment setting completed by the sound-heart criterion in 26:89.
The Book's arrival as guidance is only a general parallel to Ibrahim's coming to his Lord.
Calling upon one's Lord offers a limited devotional parallel but does not develop Ibrahim's sound heart.
It immediately identifies Ibrahim as belonging to Noah's way and introduces the focus statement.
Coming with a penitent heart closely parallels coming to God with a sound heart as an inwardly formed condition.
The call of Moses in the sacred valley does not clarify Ibrahim's arrival with a sound heart.
The blessing upon Musa and Harun is a broad prophetic honor parallel, without the focus's heart theme.

Ibrahim's submission to the Lord supplies a direct earlier expression of the undivided allegiance named in the focus.

Ibrahim's hospitality to his guests does not develop his arrival before the Lord with a sound heart.

The sleepers' bodies being turned from side to side does not clarify the moral condition of the heart.
The messengers' call to worship God alone gives the monotheistic demand embodied by Ibrahim's sound heart.
Hearts covered against the call form a direct negative contrast to Ibrahim's receptive heart.
Mary's arrival with her child before her people does not clarify the focus's inward devotion.
Wholehearted submission to God together with doing good describes the allegiance that characterizes a sound heart.
The people's turning away immediately shows the opposite response to Ibrahim's Godward integrity.
Coming with witnesses at judgment is a broad arrival-before-God parallel without the focus's heart condition.
Ayyub's plea to his Lord in affliction does not clarify Ibrahim's sound heart.
The blessing specifically upon Ibrahim presents the honored outcome of the faithfulness introduced in the focus.
Peace granted for patient endurance offers a meaningful outcome parallel to inward integrity, though not a direct lexical link.
Hearts hardened against divine distress sharply contrast with Ibrahim's heart remaining sound before his Lord.
The Paradise drink's harmlessness does not clarify the focus's heart condition.
Disease in hearts provides a general negative contrast to a sound heart.
Hearts reaching throats under siege describe fear, not the focus's stable devotion.
The reversal of worldly friendship at judgment does not clarify Ibrahim's sound heart.

Passing by the ruins in the morning does not develop the focus's inward condition.

Zakariyya's prayer for an heir does not clarify the focus's heart condition.
The one Muslim household in Lot's town offers only a general parallel of faithful submission.
The prayer to remove rancor from believers' hearts develops an inwardly clean communal heart condition.
Peace for those who follow guidance is a broad outcome parallel to sincere submission.
The accusation concerning Musa's intended violence does not clarify Ibrahim's sound heart.
Hearts sealed from hearing and sight form a strong negative contrast to the focus's uncorrupted heart.

Divine aid that reassures believers' hearts gives a related picture of hearts settled by reliance on God.

The reward for bringing the king's cup does not clarify the focus.
The magicians' return to their Lord after faith offers a limited conversion parallel.
The barren wind sent against Ad does not clarify Ibrahim's arrival or heart.
The brothers' return to their family is unrelated to coming to God with a sound heart.
Taking desire as a god and sealing the heart directly oppose Ibrahim's exclusive devotion and sound heart.
The greeting of peace across the barrier is a broad eschatological blessing parallel.
Pharaoh's wife seeks nearness to her Lord while rejecting her oppressive setting, a meaningful model of inwardly faithful allegiance.
Having a heart that receives the reminder directly identifies the living receptivity that the focus calls sound.
Believers' good assumption in response to slander loosely reflects moral cleanness but not the focus's Godward heart.
The night characterized by peace offers only a lexical and atmospheric parallel to soundness.
Ibrahim's fulfillment of his Lord's tests gives a foundational account of the proven integrity named by the sound heart.
It rejects turning away from Ibrahim's religion, directly reinforcing the faithful orientation embodied in the focus.
Ibrahim's final charge to remain submitted to God gives a direct familial expression of whole-hearted devotion.
It identifies Ibrahim as a devoted monotheist in submission to God and not among the associators.
The command to follow Ibrahim's upright religion reinforces the exemplary allegiance expressed in the focus.
Following Ibrahim's upright religion while doing good directly develops his model of sincere devotion.
Ibrahim's challenge to his father for taking idols as gods directly supplies the anti-idolatrous setting of his sound heart.
Showing Ibrahim the dominion of heaven and earth prepares the certainty underlying his undivided faith.
His refusal to treat a setting star as lord begins the reasoning that separates him from idolatry.
His rejection of the setting moon continues Ibrahim's refusal to let created signs displace the Lord.
His rejection of the setting sun completes the progressive break from created objects of worship.
Ibrahim turns his face exclusively to the Creator and expressly disavows association, directly defining his sound orientation.
Ibrahim's fearless answer to his people's dispute shows the settled trust before God implied by the focus.
He contrasts fearing false associates with fearing the God who has given proof, directly clarifying exclusive devotion.
Faith not mixed with wrongdoing is joined to security and guidance, closely paralleling the integrity of a sound heart.
The divine proof granted to Ibrahim over his people grounds the faithful stand summarized in the focus.
Ibrahim's withdrawal from seeking forgiveness for his father establishes the limit of loyalty when it conflicts with God.
Ibrahim's prayer for protection from worshipping idols directly expresses the monotheistic preservation of his inner state.
His prayer that hearts incline toward the sacred house develops a God-directed heart orientation.
Ibrahim is described as devoutly obedient, upright, and free of association, a close characterization of the focus's sound heart.
His gratitude and divine guidance reinforce the stable faithfulness ascribed to Ibrahim.
The command to follow Ibrahim's upright religion directly presents his monotheism as an enduring model.
Ibrahim is named truthful and a prophet, directly supporting the integrity of his presentation before the Lord.
His appeal to his father not to worship what cannot hear, see, or benefit directly develops the focus narrative.
Ibrahim tells his father that revealed knowledge has come and calls him to follow it, showing principled fidelity over inherited practice.
The warning not to worship Satan extends Ibrahim's rejection of his father's idolatrous path.
His warning about remaining allied with Satan shows the moral seriousness of the father's religious choice.
The father's threat makes explicit the familial pressure against which Ibrahim maintains faithful conviction.
Ibrahim's restrained response to his hostile father displays integrity within the same religious conflict.
His separation from his father and what he invokes besides God directly models exclusive allegiance to the Lord.
The gift of Isaac and Jacob follows Ibrahim's separation for God, giving the narrative consequence of that fidelity.
God says Ibrahim had already been given right guidance and was known by Him, directly framing the soundness in the focus.
Ibrahim's question to his father and people about their idols opens the same direct challenge to false worship.
His confession that the Lord of heaven and earth is their Lord gives the positive creed underlying his rejection of idols.
His resolve to act against the idols advances the decisive break with his people's worship.
The idolaters' return to self-recognition gives a contrasting moment of inward reckoning provoked by Ibrahim's challenge.
Ibrahim's question about worshipping what neither benefits nor harms exposes the incoherence of idolatry.
His rebuke of idol worship intensifies the exclusive monotheism that the focus presupposes.
The religion of Ibrahim is named as the inherited way in which believers are called Muslims, extending his model of submission.
The command to recite Ibrahim's account introduces the extended narrative that explains his monotheistic integrity.
Ibrahim declares himself free of all objects of worship except the Lord of the worlds, directly defining exclusive devotion.
His confession that the Lord created and guides him gives the positive basis of his Godward heart.
Ibrahim's reliance on the Lord for food and drink develops his complete dependence on God.
His attribution of healing to God further displays undivided trust in the Lord.
His attribution of death and life to God reinforces the total divine lordship he embraces.
His hope that the Lord will forgive him on the Day of Judgment gives an explicit account-facing orientation to God.
Ibrahim's call to worship and fear God directly states the allegiance represented by his sound heart.
His exposure of idols as fabrications develops the same rejection of false worship found in the surrounding focus narrative.
Ibrahim's declaration that he is emigrating to his Lord closely parallels the focus's coming to his Lord.
His advance toward the idols immediately continues the practical rejection of the worship he confronts after the focus.
His question to the idols exposes their incapacity and sharpens the anti-idolatrous content of his sound heart.
Ibrahim's challenge to worship what people carve directly identifies the false worship his sound heart refuses.
The declaration that God created both people and what they make gives the theological ground for rejecting idols.
Their failed plot against Ibrahim and his elevation display the vindication of his faithful stand.
Ibrahim's declaration that he is going to his Lord and will be guided is the closest local parallel to the focus's coming to his Lord.
His prayer for righteous offspring continues the God-dependent orientation of Ibrahim's narrative.
The announcement of a forbearing son prepares the later test but does not itself clarify the sound heart.
The shared readiness of Ibrahim and his son for the commanded sacrifice enacts the steadfast submission associated with the focus.
Ibrahim's inclusion among God's chosen servants extends the portrait of his exemplary fidelity.
Their purification for remembrance of the final abode supplies a related account of inwardly directed devotion.
Their status among the chosen and excellent reinforces the favorable evaluation of Ibrahim's character.
Ibrahim's declaration of disassociation from what his people worship directly parallels the focus narrative's rejection of idols.
His exception for the One who created him gives the same exclusive Creator-centered orientation as the sound heart.
The enduring word among his descendants extends Ibrahim's monotheistic commitment beyond the immediate scene.
Ibrahim's fulfillment provides a concise parallel to tested faithfulness before God.
Ibrahim and his companions explicitly disavow their people's worship and affirm enmity until belief in God alone, directly modeling exclusive devotion.
Their prayer to the Lord for reliance, forgiveness, and protection develops the Godward trust of Ibrahim's community.
Ibrahim and his companions are presented as an excellent example for those hoping in God and the Last Day.
